game-auth-bypass.intro: Identify the flaw and why it matters.

challenges.q: A login sets a cookie role=admin for admins. Flaw?
a: Client-controlled authorisation, trivially changed to admin
challenges.why: A cookie the client can edit must never hold a privilege decision.

challenges.q: Password reset link contains reset_token=base64(username+timestamp). Flaw?
a: Predictable and forgeable for any user
challenges.why: Encoded is not signed. Anyone can mint a token for any account.

challenges.q: The JWT header accepts alg none and the server honours it. Impact?
a: Tokens can be forged with no signature
challenges.why: If the header selects the verification method, an attacker selects none.

challenges.q: Login errors differ: user not found versus invalid password. Flaw?
challenges.why: It reveals which accounts exist before any password attack.

challenges.q: The session ID is unchanged after login. Flaw?
challenges.why: An attacker who pre-set the ID now shares the authenticated session.

challenges.q: Password reset step 2 accepts a new password without rechecking the step 1 token. Flaw?
a: Broken flow, reset any account by skipping validation
challenges.why: Each step must independently validate the previous authorisation.

challenges.q: An admin endpoint hides its button in JavaScript. Flaw?
a: The endpoint is unprotected; the UI is not a control
challenges.why: Hiding the button is cosmetic. The request still succeeds.

challenges.q: A JWT is signed with the secret 'secret123'. Flaw?
a: Weak secret, crackable offline to forge tokens for any user
challenges.why: Recovering the signing key means minting any token.

game-ecb-detect.intro: Which mode produced this, and how can you tell?

challenges.q: Ciphertext blocks: block1 equals block4 of the same message. Which mode?
challenges.why: Identical ciphertext blocks mean identical plaintext encrypted independently, which is ECB.

challenges.q: Why is ECB unsuitable even for encrypted data at rest?
a: Identical plaintext blocks leak structure and patterns
challenges.why: Repeated data produces repeated ciphertext, which is observable.

challenges.q: Which mode needs a unique IV and provides authentication?
challenges.why: GCM is authenticated encryption and requires a nonce that is never reused.

challenges.q: In CBC, what does a padding oracle let an attacker do?
a: Decrypt ciphertext byte by byte using the error signal
challenges.why: The oracle reveals whether padding is valid, which leaks plaintext one byte at a time.

challenges.q: Which mode turns a block cipher into a stream cipher?
challenges.why: CTR generates a keystream and XORs it, so reusing the nonce breaks it.

challenges.q: A TLS record shows TLS 1.0 negotiated while the client offered 1.3. What might this indicate?
a: A downgrade attempt or a very old server
challenges.why: Choosing the oldest offered version is the signature of a downgrade.

challenges.q: Target: POST /email/change with email field. No CSRF token, cookie not SameSite. Which payload works?
items: An auto-submitting form POSTing the email field
An img tag pointing at the endpoint
An anchor the user must click
challenges.why: An auto-submitting form is the standard CSRF payload. img only works for GET, and fetch is blocked cross-origin without CORS.

challenges.q: Same target but it accepts GET. Simplest payload?
items: A single img tag with the parameters in the query string
challenges.why: A state-changing GET falls to one image tag, which is why state changes must be POST.

challenges.q: The session cookie is SameSite=Lax and the action is POST. Does it work?
items: No, Lax blocks cross-site POST; only a top-level GET navigation would send it
challenges.why: Lax permits top-level GET navigations but not cross-site POSTs or subresource requests.

challenges.q: A token is present but identical for every user and never expires. Does the defence hold?
items: No, an attacker can fetch their own token and reuse it
challenges.why: The token must be bound to the session and unpredictable to provide any protection.

challenges.q: The request is JSON and the API only accepts Content-Type application/json. Why does this help?
items: Simple cross-site form posts cannot set that content type, so no CORS preflight passes
challenges.why: Requiring a content type that forms cannot produce forces a preflight, which the server can then refuse.

game-secure-review.intro: Find the vulnerability in the snippet and pick the real fix.

challenges.q: Python: cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '%s'" % name). Fix?
a: cursor.execute with a parameter placeholder and a tuple of values
challenges.why: Parameters separate the query structure from the data at the protocol level.

challenges.q:
Node: res.send(`

Hello ${req.query.name}

`). Fix?
a: Escape or template-render the value with autoescaping
challenges.why: Contextual output encoding from a template engine that escapes by default removes the class of bug.

challenges.q: PHP: include($_GET[page]). Fix?
a: Validate against an allowlist of permitted pages
challenges.why: Allowlisting removes arbitrary path and wrapper input entirely.

challenges.q: Java: getConnection(user, pass, ADMIN_PASSWORD_HARDCODED). Fix?
a: Load from a secret store or environment
challenges.why: Secrets belong outside source, loaded at runtime, and rotated on exposure.

challenges.q: An endpoint takes userId from the request body and returns that user record after checking the caller is authenticated. Fix?
a: Derive the user from the session, or verify the caller may access that specific object
challenges.why: Authentication is not authorisation. The object-level check is missing.

challenges.q: A password is stored as md5(password). Fix?
a: Use bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2 with a per-user salt
challenges.why: Fast general-purpose hashes are wrong for passwords regardless of digest length.

challenges.q: A shell command: os.system("ping " + host). Fix?
a: Use an argument array with a library that does not invoke a shell
challenges.why: Removing the shell removes the interpretation of metacharacters entirely.

challenges.q: An API returns a stack trace with the database schema on error. Fix?
a: Return a generic error to the client and log detail server-side
challenges.why: Verbose errors are reconnaissance, and the detail belongs in logs only.

challenges.q: A JWT is verified without checking the exp claim. Fix?
a: Validate exp, iss and aud, and enforce the expected algorithm
challenges.why: Without expiry validation a stolen token is valid forever.

challenges.q: A file upload saves to the web root with the user-supplied filename. Fix?
a: Store outside the web root with a generated name and validate content type and size
challenges.why: Not reachable and not executable makes any stored content inert.
